meta.storyTitle: Isolate reviewer access and fetch dependency advisories

summary.prose: This Story checks a repository's dependencies against public advisories while confining what each package manager can read, execute, and transmit. Every audit runs against an isolated, disposable copy of exactly the files it needs (never the live repository tree), pinned to the moment that copy is made so the reported content identity cannot drift from what was actually audited. Each manager is driven through a documented, concrete invocation that avoids dependency resolution and code execution where the tool allows it (pip/pipenv/poetry via pip-audit's --no-deps --require-hashes mode; cargo audit's local-comparison, no-disclosure design) and pins network egress to the one destination that manager's own configuration supports, verified by a negative-access probe before any manager is trusted. A manager, dependency or source that cannot be scoped, confined, or verified this way is reported as an explicit gap -- never silently skipped, never run against the live tree, and never accepted on an unverified assumption.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic adds a standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/) that owns model selection, dependency-advisory collection, code-assessment execution, and reporting, and supplies review-round's existing RoundDriverHooks.security hook as a thin adapter. review-round itself stays unchanged except for the one call site invoking that hook; the data shapes it already exports (SecurityFinding, SecurityLocator, EvidenceProvider, VerificationReceipt) are populated, never redefined.

ownedContracts.name: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
ownedContracts.purpose: Carries s2's dependency-advisory collection outcome (controller-side, no model) across the boundary: the pinned contentIdentity it was collected against (so s3 can verify it recomputes/matches the same identity before trusting this evidence), the queried coordinates, the actual advisory matches with affected versions and provenance, the per-match advisory destination enforced (not merely observed), the per-manager input mode used (manifest-scoped | isolated-environment | confined-source-copy | unsupported), and the dependencies/sources that stayed unresolved, unavailable or unsupported -- so s3 can report confirmed affected dependencies and unverified coverage as DISTINCT values bound to the SAME content identity as its own code findings.

boundary.internal: pkg_audit's package-manager resolution; the ENFORCED (not merely recorded) per-manager network boundary -- blocking any request to an unapproved destination before it leaves the process, including redirects and a tool's own secondary requests, and refusing to run a manager's audit at all when that enforcement cannot be established; the documented per-manager input/mode mapping (npm/pnpm/yarn/cargo: manifest+lockfile scope; pip/pipenv/poetry: an isolated environment resolved from the pinned manifest, never the ambient active environment pip-audit defaults to; go: a confined copy of the pinned snapshot's module source, since govulncheck performs source-level analysis, not a manifest read) with an explicit coverage gap for any manager s2 cannot correctly scope under that mapping; and the advisory-match collection that populates SecurityAdvisoryEvidence (stamped with the pinned contentIdentity) stay private to s2. No model, tool-loop, or CLI session is involved in s2 at all. ac2's gap-reporting distinguishes a SUCCESSFUL audit that found vulnerabilities (a valid, parseable result regardless of exit code -- pkg_audit's own auditArgv already marks every supported manager nonZeroOk:true) from an EXECUTION GAP (spawn failure, unparseable output, an unsupported manager, or a manager s2's input/mode mapping cannot correctly scope) -- these are never conflated.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Model-tier resolution (extending src/config/role-taxonomy.ts with a security role), availability/credential checks, and the no-silent-fallback blocker-reporting logic stay private to s1; only the resolved SecurityModelSelection crosses its boundary. s1 must also specify the configuration contract for an INDEPENDENTLY selectable security-model binding (distinct from core/mid/cheap) and its interaction with coreFloor enforcement and unavailable-model handling; this is s1's central, still-open design question.

The RoundDriverHooks.security adapter function; the CliProvider.runReadOnlySession dispatch of the code-vulnerability pass against the SAME pinned contentIdentity s2 collected against (recomputed/verified by s3, refusing on a mismatch), using s1's resolved model, under a backend REQUIRED to deny credential-location reads, out-of-scope reads and unauthorized MCP operations -- verified per backend by an actual negative-access test (not merely confirming a restricting flag was passed), with s3 refusing to dispatch through a backend that cannot be so verified; the exact per-provider mechanism is an s3 LLD decision, the three denials and the refuse-if-unverifiable rule are fixed here. The call into runReviewRound and the separate ownership of everything runReviewRound itself does NOT do (sandbox/mutation checkpoint execution, round reconciliation, VerificationReceipt persistence, and checkpoint cleanup); the mapping from the review's pinned contentIdentity onto the epicHash/storyId identity persistVerificationReceipt requires; and the assembly of SecurityFinding/SecurityEvidence plus a supplemental report structure stay private to s3. It consumes s1's SecurityModelSelection and s2's SecurityAdvisoryEvidence to produce that report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A -- foundational contracts (model selection and enforced advisory collection)

nonFunctional.security: The per-manager network boundary in s2 is ENFORCED before any request leaves the process (blocking unapproved destinations, redirects and a tool's own secondary requests), not merely observed and recorded afterward; a manager for which that boundary cannot be established is refused, not run unconfined. s2's filesystem/environment scope follows a documented per-manager mode (manifest-scoped for npm/pnpm/yarn/cargo; an isolated resolved environment for pip/pipenv/poetry, since pip-audit otherwise audits the ambient active environment; a confined source copy for go, since govulncheck performs source-level analysis) -- a manager outside that mapping is an explicit coverage gap, never a best-effort run against the wrong target. This is SEPARATE from the configured CLI model's own inference traffic (k1: routes through the installed CLI provider), which is expected and unrelated to dependency-advisory egress. s3's code-vulnerability pass is dispatched only through a CLI backend REQUIRED to deny credential-location reads, out-of-scope reads (outside the pinned contentIdentity), and unauthorized MCP operations -- each denial verified by a real negative-access test, not by checking that a flag exists; a backend that cannot be so verified is refused. The exact per-provider enforcement mechanism for both s2's and s3's boundaries is an s2/s3 LLD decision; the invariants, the owners, and the refuse-if-unenforceable rule are fixed by this HLD.
nonFunctional.observability: Every checkpoint run -- pass or fail, whether or not a SecurityFinding corroborates it -- is recorded as a VerificationReceipt (already built, src/workflow/review-round/receipt-record.ts), so a security review's execution is auditable independent of its findings. s3 owns stamping that record with the epicHash/storyId persistVerificationReceipt requires, mapped from the review's own pinned contentIdentity.
nonFunctional.durability: No new persistent storage is introduced for s1/s2's own outputs (SecurityModelSelection, SecurityAdvisoryEvidence are transient per-review values); the durable records are the already-typed SecurityFinding/VerificationReceipt heads the shared round-driver machinery (Epic 03f4fd3b9102aab8) persists, plus s3's new supplemental report structure (not yet a stored artifact type; its persistence mechanism is an open question for the s3 LLD).
nonFunctional.performance: Not a stated constraint for this Epic; the new module's cost is bounded by one pkg_audit invocation (per confined manager) and one CLI read-only session per request, not a new background job.

api.name: computeContentIdentity
api.signature: function computeContentIdentity(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<string>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The registered repo root git_rev_parse/git_status run against, and the base every targets.entries path is resolved and validated against -- removes the ambiguity of a relative path across two registered repos (revision-1 gap).

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The round's submitter-owned content list (artifact-core/types.ts:345-347); computeContentIdentity expands each manager's COMPLETE required input set (see requiredInputsForManager) around these entries, not just the single path named.

returns.meaning: A deterministic digest over the repo's HEAD commit sha (via git_rev_parse) plus a sha256 (Node's own crypto, not git_hash_object) of every dirty/untracked file's raw bytes within the complete, per-manager input set -- computed in the SAME pass that materializes the isolated audit copy (see the materialization entity below), so there is no window between 'hash computed' and 'bytes audited' for the live repo to change in. s3 recomputes the same function independently against the same repoPath/targets to verify it reviewed the same content.

errors.condition: the target repository's git state cannot be read (not a git repository, repoPath not registered, or the underlying git_rev_parse/git_status calls fail)
a targets.entries path resolves outside repoPath

preconditions: repoPath is a registered repo root with a resolvable HEAD
postconditions: pure function of the repo's current git state, repoPath and targets.entries -- calling it twice with no intervening change to the complete per-manager input set yields the identical string
never includes file content from outside repoPath or the complete per-manager input set

hashes raw file bytes directly (crypto.createHash('sha256') over the file read from disk) -- never delegates to git_hash_object, which applies git attribute clean filters before hashing and can collide on different raw content

api.name: collectDependencyAdvisories
api.signature: function collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<SecurityAdvisoryEvidence>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Same registered repo root as computeContentIdentity; also the root enumerateManagers walks to find every manifest in scope.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: Bounds which manifests/managers are in scope for this collection, same as computeContentIdentity's targets.

returns.meaning: sc2's full result: contentIdentity (via computeContentIdentity), queriedCoordinates, matches, perManagerMode, unresolvedDependencies, and unavailableSources.

preconditions: enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) has found at least an attempt-worthy manifest, or the result is an all-gaps SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
postconditions: every manager it attempts runs ONLY against the isolated, materialized copy created in the same pass as its contentIdentity hashing -- never against the live repoPath tree directly, for any manager

never sends a manager's traffic anywhere but that manager's own documented, pinned destination, and only after a negative-access probe confirms a disallowed decoy destination is unreachable via that manager's own configured path; a manager whose enforcement cannot be verified is recorded in perManagerMode as 'unsupported' and is never actually run
every queried coordinate ends up in exactly one of matches or unresolvedDependencies (or contributes to a 'no findings' result) -- never silently dropped
the returned contentIdentity equals computeContentIdentity(repoPath, targets) called over the exact same materialized input set each manager actually audited
never throws -- every manager-level failure becomes an explicit perManagerMode/unavailableSources/unresolvedDependencies entry, not an exception, matching ac2's 'remain explicit gaps' requirement

api.name: createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Captured in the returned provider's closure and forwarded to collectDependencyAdvisories on every run() call, since EvidenceProvider.run's own fixed signature (evidence-provider.ts:26-40) carries no repo-identity field.

returns.meaning: An object with category:'dependency-sbom' whose run(input) calls collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath, input.targets) and maps its matches into the thin EvidenceProviderOutput.evidence (one SecurityEvidence per match, providerCategory:'dependency-sbom', locator pointing at the matched coordinate's manifest file). The richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence itself is NOT part of this return value -- the orchestration module obtains sc2 directly by calling collectDependencyAdvisories, not through the registry.

postconditions: the returned object satisfies the EvidenceProvider interface exactly (evidence-provider.ts:26-40), so the existing EvidenceProviderRegistry can hold it under the 'dependency-sbom' key unchanged

dataModelChanges.details: Add one optional `env?: Record<string, string>` property to pkgAuditTool's inputSchema, forwarded straight to runShell's existing per-call options.env (shell-helper.ts:40,103,181) inside execute() -- purely additive; no existing caller passes `env` today. `cwd` (already an accepted input) is pointed at the isolated materialized copy for every manager, never the live repo tree.

dataModelChanges.entity: auditArgv's pipenv/poetry cases -- switched to pip-audit against a generated hash-pinned requirements file
dataModelChanges.details: CURRENT INVARIANT BEING REPLACED: auditArgv's pipenv case runs `pipenv check --output json` and its poetry case runs `poetry audit` (pkg/index.ts:164-175) -- each manager's OWN native audit command, run against whatever environment that command resolves on its own. NEW behavior: pipenv/poetry's audit path is switched to the SAME pip-audit invocation pip itself uses (`pip-audit -r <generated requirements> --no-deps --require-hashes -f json`), where `<generated requirements>` is produced by this Story from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock's own pinned {name, version, hash} triples -- both lockfiles already carry hashes, so no new resolution is needed to produce it. This is a deliberate, additive-only-at-the-manager-level change to pkg_audit's existing exported behavior for manager:'pipenv'|'poetry' specifically; npm/pnpm/yarn/go/cargo/plain-pip cases are untouched.

dataModelChanges.entity: Repository-root threading (repoPath) through computeContentIdentity, collectDependencyAdvisories, createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider
dataModelChanges.details: ReviewTargets carries no repository identity (entries are bare paths -- artifact-core/types.ts:345-347), so a relative path like package.json is ambiguous across two registered repos sharing that relative path. Every s2-owned function now takes an explicit repoPath (a registered repo root); every targets.entries path is validated as resolving inside repoPath before use, and git_rev_parse/git_status/the manifest enumerator all run with repoPath as their base, never the daemon's own ambient process.cwd().

dataModelChanges.entity: requiredInputsForManager + isolated materialization (replaces the revision-1 'mode preparer')
dataModelChanges.details: requiredInputsForManager(manager) names the COMPLETE set of files that manager's audit genuinely needs, not just the single manifest path a caller might name: npm/pnpm/yarn -> {package.json, the matching lockfile}; cargo -> {Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock}; pip (hash-pinned requirements only) -> {the hash-pinned requirements file}; pipenv -> {Pipfile, Pipfile.lock}; poetry -> {pyproject.toml, poetry.lock}; go -> {go.mod, go.sum} plus the module source tree govulncheck's source-level analysis needs. For EVERY manager, that complete set (never anything else from repoPath) is copied byte-for-byte into a fresh, disposable temp directory in the SAME pass computeContentIdentity hashes those same bytes -- closing the gap where a later audit could read content that changed after hashing (revision-1's TOCTOU gap) and guaranteeing the hash set is actually complete (revision-1 only hashed the single named path, missing e.g. a sibling lockfile). Every manager's pkg_audit invocation runs with `cwd` pointed at this temp copy -- never repoPath directly, and never an ambient install/venv outside it.

dataModelChanges.entity: Per-manager destination pin + negative-access verification (replaces the revision-1 generic allowlisting proxy + decoy probe)
dataModelChanges.details: Each manager is pinned to the ONE network destination its OWN configuration surface supports, rather than relying on an env-var proxy a tool might ignore: npm/pnpm/yarn -> `--registry <the one approved registry>` (a native CLI flag, not env-var proxying); cargo -> `audit.toml`'s db-url pinned to the single official RustSec advisory-db git remote; pip-audit (hash-pinned mode) -> its own `--index-url`-equivalent pinned to one approved index/OSV source; go -> `GOPROXY` pinned to the one approved module proxy with `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly` (refuses any go.mod/go.sum change). Before trusting ANY manager, run a per-manager-type NEGATIVE-access probe (cached per manager type, not just a single decoy-reachable check): confirm that pointing the SAME manager at a disallowed decoy destination, through that manager's own configured path, demonstrably fails -- not merely that the approved destination is reachable. A manager with a KNOWN auxiliary network path its own configuration cannot bound (e.g. an undocumented telemetry call) is refused outright (perManagerMode 'unsupported'), and this residual limitation -- no OS-level network-namespace/sandbox enforcement exists in this codebase, so a manager's native tool spawning an unconfigured subprocess or secondary client is NOT independently blockable -- is stated explicitly, never silently assumed away.

dataModelChanges.entity: Per-manager disclosure profile (resolves the 'approved coordinates' requirement honestly per manager)
dataModelChanges.details: Documents, per manager, exactly what crosses the pinned destination, since 'send only approved coordinates' cannot be uniformly true for every native audit command: npm/pnpm/yarn's own audit command can disclose the FULL lockfile dependency tree plus CLI/platform metadata to its one pinned registry (npm's own documented Quick Audit fallback payload) -- an accepted, explicitly recorded disclosure to that single approved destination, not a coordinate-only one; cargo audit discloses NOTHING over the network (the advisory comparison runs locally against the cloned RustSec database after one git fetch) -- the strongest case; pip-audit in --no-deps --require-hashes mode discloses name+version+hash per pinned requirement, never a full environment dump; go discloses the module path+version coordinates GOPROXY needs to fetch content already hash-verified by go.sum. Each SecurityAdvisoryMatch.advisoryDestination plus this documented disclosure profile is what s3 and the final report rely on -- never a blanket 'coordinates only' claim pkg_audit's wrapped native tools cannot actually keep for every manager.

dataModelChanges.entity: enumerateManagers (replaces reliance on detectManager's single-match precedence)
dataModelChanges.details: detectManager(cwd) (pkg/index.ts) returns only the FIRST manager it finds via a fixed lockfile precedence order, stopping at the first match -- it never enumerates co-located managers (e.g. a Python requirements.txt beside an npm package.json in the same directory) or nested project directories. enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) instead walks every manifest/lockfile signal within repoPath bounded by targets.entries' own directories, producing one {manager, manifestDir} pair per manifest found; two different managers' manifests in two different directories are each audited independently, while two conflicting manifests in the SAME directory for the SAME manager family are flagged as an unresolved ambiguity rather than guessed at.

Translates each manager's own result shape (npm/pnpm's parsed JSON, pip-audit's JSON, cargo audit's JSON; yarn/go's non-JSON text output, since auditArgv marks them expectsJson:false) into the common SecurityAdvisoryMatch[] shape (coordinate, advisoryId, affectedVersions, severity, provenance, advisoryDestination). An unparseable or malformed result is recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap, never silently treated as 'no findings' -- distinct from a successful audit that legitimately found nothing.

The HLD-defined output record this Story owns, produced by collectDependencyAdvisories exactly as the HLD's interfaceSketch specifies: { contentIdentity, readOnly: true, queriedCoordinates, matches: SecurityAdvisoryMatch[], perManagerMode, unresolvedDependencies, unavailableSources }. Lives in the Epic's new standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/), and crosses the s2->s3 boundary unchanged.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: collectDependencyAdvisories is the sole producer of SecurityAdvisoryEvidence. For every manager enumerateManagers finds, it materializes that manager's COMPLETE required input set into an isolated temp copy (hashing those exact bytes into contentIdentity in the same pass), pins that manager's audit to its own documented single destination, verifies that pin with a negative-access probe, and -- only if verified -- runs pkg_audit against the isolated copy and maps its output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[] with an honest, per-manager disclosure profile. Every unresolved/unavailable/unsupported case is recorded explicitly rather than dropped. s3 consumes the returned value directly (not through the EvidenceProvider registry) to recompute and verify contentIdentity before trusting the evidence, and to report confirmed affected dependencies vs. unverified coverage as distinct values in its own report.

errorCases.scenario: A manager's negative-access probe fails: pointing it at a disallowed decoy destination through its own configured path still succeeds, meaning its enforcement cannot be verified (e.g. a manager that does not honor its own documented proxy/registry/index configuration).
errorCases.detection: The per-manager-type negative-access probe (run before any audit for that manager type) observes the decoy destination being reached when it should have been refused.
errorCases.response: That manager's perManagerMode is recorded 'unsupported'; pkg_audit is never invoked for it at all, and its coordinates are added to unresolvedDependencies instead.
errorCases.userImpact: No uncontrolled egress ever occurs for a manager whose destination-pinning cannot be verified; the report explains exactly why that manager's dependencies are unresolved.

errorCases.scenario: Materializing a manager's complete required input set (requiredInputsForManager) into the isolated temp copy fails -- a required sibling file (e.g. the lockfile beside the manifest) is missing or unreadable.
errorCases.detection: The materialization step's own file-copy/read fails before any hashing or audit begins for that manager.
errorCases.response: That manager's perManagerMode is recorded 'unsupported'; no partial copy is ever audited, and no fallback to the live repoPath tree occurs.
errorCases.userImpact: Never audits an incomplete or substituted input set silently; the gap is explicit.

errorCases.scenario: pkg_audit's underlying CLI binary is not installed for a manager that DID pass its negative-access probe (e.g. pip-audit itself is missing).
errorCases.detection: runShell's existing r.spawnError flag (pkg/index.ts:487-489's existing check) surfaces back to collectDependencyAdvisories.
errorCases.response: That manager is recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap, never conflated with 'no findings reported'.
errorCases.userImpact: Distinguishes 'the audit tool is genuinely absent' from 'the audit ran and found nothing.'

errorCases.scenario: A manager's audit output is unparseable or malformed in a way distinct from pkg_audit's normal nonZeroOk:true 'findings reported' convention (e.g. expectsJson:true but JSON.parse fails, or an unexpected text shape for a non-JSON manager).
errorCases.detection: The per-manager raw-output-to-SecurityAdvisoryMatch mapper fails to extract any usable fields from r.stdout.
errorCases.response: Recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap; never silently reported as a clean, findings-free result.
errorCases.userImpact: A parse failure never masquerades as a successful security check.

errorCases.scenario: A bare `pip` manifest (requirements.txt with no Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock) does not have per-dependency hashes, so --require-hashes --no-deps cannot run without either failing outright or falling back to resolution (which can execute setup.py).
errorCases.detection: The generated-requirements step checks every line for a --hash pin before invoking pip-audit; an unhashed requirements.txt fails this check.
errorCases.response: Plain 'pip' with an unhashed manifest is recorded perManagerMode 'unsupported' -- never falls back to resolving or installing to make the audit possible.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently executes third-party setup.py code just to make an audit possible; the coverage gap is explicit instead.

errorCases.scenario: Two different package-manager manifests for the SAME manager family are found in the same directory under repoPath (e.g. two conflicting lockfiles enumerateManagers cannot disambiguate).
errorCases.detection: enumerateManagers detects more than one candidate manifest for the same manager family in one directory.
errorCases.response: That directory's manager is recorded as an unresolved ambiguity (added to unresolvedDependencies with a note), never guessed at by picking one arbitrarily.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently audits the wrong lockfile when two plausible ones exist.

edgeCases.input: A manager's audit legitimately exits non-zero with a fully parseable 'findings reported' result (pkg_audit's own existing nonZeroOk:true convention for every manager).
edgeCases.expected: Treated as a SUCCESSFUL audit -- matches populated from the parsed result, NOT an execution gap, preserving ac2's own distinction and pkg_audit's existing behavior unchanged.

edgeCases.input: No manifest for a given manager is present anywhere under repoPath within targets.entries' directories (that manager simply is not used by this repo).
edgeCases.expected: That manager is never attempted and its absence is not reported as an unavailableSource or unresolvedDependency -- correctly out of scope, not a gap.

edgeCases.input: The same coordinate name happens to appear via two different managers in two different directories in the same review.
edgeCases.expected: Each manager's match is recorded independently in matches, keyed by its own manager-scoped coordinate; no de-duplication that could hide one manager's distinct finding.

edgeCases.input: A dirty/untracked file within a manager's complete required input set has git attributes that would apply a clean filter (e.g. line-ending normalization) if hashed via git_hash_object.
edgeCases.expected: computeContentIdentity hashes the file's raw bytes directly via Node's crypto, bypassing git attribute filters entirely, so the digest reflects exactly what is copied into the isolated materialization and audited -- never a filter-transformed value.

edgeCases.input: cargo audit's advisory-database git fetch succeeds but finds the local clone already up to date (no new commits).
edgeCases.expected: Still counted as a successful, verified fetch against the one pinned remote -- not treated as a failure merely because nothing changed.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test (node --test) with node:assert, matching the daemon tools convention this Story's own pkg_audit change sits beside (e.g. src/daemon/tools/__tests__/approval-broker.test.ts's `import test from 'node:test'` pattern).

testLevels.purpose: Prove computeContentIdentity's determinism, scoping, and raw-byte hashing in isolation, with a fake git-plumbing layer (no real git_rev_parse/git_status subprocess calls) and real Node crypto over fixture bytes.
subjects: computeContentIdentity: identical HEAD sha + identical complete-input-set bytes -> identical string on repeated calls
computeContentIdentity: a change to a dirty file's raw bytes within the complete input set -> a different string
computeContentIdentity: a change to a file OUTSIDE the complete input set -> no change to the string
computeContentIdentity: a targets.entries path resolving outside repoPath -> throws

computeContentIdentity: a file with git attributes that would apply a clean filter -> the digest reflects the RAW bytes, not the filtered content (a fixture repo with a .gitattributes clean filter, comparing computeContentIdentity's result against the raw file bytes hashed independently)
computeContentIdentity: git state unreadable (not a git repo) -> throws the documented Error

materialization: the hash computed during materialization matches a hash computed independently over the copy's own bytes afterward

collectDependencyAdvisories: unparseable/malformed output -> recorded in unavailableSources, never reported as 'no findings'

fixturesNeeded: a fake pkg_audit invocation (controllable exit code / stdout / spawnError per manager) standing in for the real pkgAuditTool.execute call
a fake negative-access probe returning pass/fail per manager type on command

repoPath fixtures with varying manifest combinations (npm+pip in separate dirs, go-only, no manifest, duplicate coordinate names across managers, Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock fixtures for the pip-audit substitution path)

testLevels.purpose: Prove createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider's registry-contract mapping -- the thin EvidenceProviderOutput must stay distinct from the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence.
subjects: createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider(repoPath).category === 'dependency-sbom'

createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider(repoPath).run(input) maps each SecurityAdvisoryMatch into one SecurityEvidence with providerCategory:'dependency-sbom' and a locator pointing at the matched coordinate's manifest file

the EvidenceProviderOutput never carries advisoryId/affectedVersions/severity/provenance/advisoryDestination directly -- those stay in the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence obtained separately via collectDependencyAdvisories

testLevels.purpose: Prove pkgAuditTool's new, additive `env` input is forwarded correctly and does not change behavior for any caller that omits it.
subjects: pkgAuditTool.execute: no `env` provided -> runShell is called exactly as before (process.env unchanged), matching existing behavior for every current caller
pkgAuditTool.execute: `env` provided -> runShell is called with that exact env object, not merged silently with process.env in a way that could leak unrelated variables
pkgAuditTool.execute: manager:'pipenv'/'poetry' now invokes pip-audit against the generated hash-pinned requirements file, not `pipenv check`/`poetry audit`

testLevels.purpose: Prove at least one manager's destination pin and negative-access probe actually confine real traffic end-to-end against a real subprocess, and that cargo audit's local-comparison design discloses nothing -- gated behind INSRC_LIVE_TESTS=1 per the project's existing live-service-test convention.

fixturesNeeded: real npm and cargo manifest fixture repos, run only under INSRC_LIVE_TESTS=1

collectDependencyAdvisories: a bare pip requirements.txt with no hash pins -> perManagerMode 'unsupported', never falls back to resolving/installing
pkgAuditTool.execute: no `env` provided -> runShell is called exactly as before (process.env unchanged), matching existing behavior for every current caller

collectDependencyAdvisories against a real npm manifest: the audit's traffic goes only to the pinned registry, and a decoy destination outside that pin is confirmed unreachable via npm's own configured path

collectDependencyAdvisories against a real cargo manifest: no package coordinate is ever transmitted over the network (only the one advisory-db git fetch occurs), confirmed by observing the actual network calls made

alternativesConsidered.name: Minimal additive pkg_audit env override + per-call ephemeral allowlisting proxy
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add one optional `env` field to pkgAuditTool's existing inputSchema (cwd is already there), forwarded to runShell's own per-call env option; s2's orchestration module starts a short-lived allowlisting proxy and per-manager scoped cwd/env for exactly the duration of one audit call.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend pkgAuditTool's inputSchema/execute with an optional `env?: Record<string,string>` passed straight to runShell's existing options.env (shell-helper.ts:40,103) -- a single additive field, not a behavior change to any existing caller. s2's own module: (1) computes contentIdentity (git_rev_parse + git_status + git_hash_object); (2) for each manager in scope, prepares its per-manager mode (npm/pnpm/yarn/cargo: pkg_audit's existing `cwd` points at the manifest directly; pip/pipenv/poetry: materialize an isolated environment resolved from the pinned manifest, pass its path via `cwd`/`env`; go: materialize a confined copy of the pinned source, pass via `cwd`); (3) starts one ephemeral local allowlisting proxy scoped to this single audit call, verifies the manager actually respects it via a decoy-destination probe, and calls pkgAuditTool.execute with `env` set to route that manager's traffic through the proxy; a manager that fails the probe is refused (coverage gap), never run unconfined; (4) maps pkg_audit's raw per-manager `parsed` output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[], and (5) wraps the whole result into both the thin EvidenceProviderOutput (for the dependency-sbom registry contract) and the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence (sc2, returned directly for s3).
pros: Reuses pkg_audit's existing tool contract almost unchanged -- one additive, optional field, no change to any other caller's behavior, directly satisfying ac2's 'not a new fetcher' requirement
The proxy and env are scoped to exactly one subprocess call (runShell's per-call options.env), so concurrent unrelated audits or other daemon work in the same process are never affected
Matches the HLD's own performance note ('bounded by one pkg_audit invocation... not a new background job') -- the proxy is ephemeral, started and torn down per call
cons: s2 still has to build real net-new machinery (the proxy itself, the per-manager mode preparers, the per-manager verification probe, the raw-output-to-SecurityAdvisoryMatch mapper) -- this is genuinely the Story's substance, not something pkg_audit already provides
Starting and tearing down a fresh local proxy per manager per review adds a small but real per-call startup cost

alternativesConsidered.name: A wholly separate scoped-audit fetcher bypassing pkg_audit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Build a new, standalone dependency-advisory fetcher that duplicates argv-building and subprocess invocation for each manager itself, instead of calling pkgAuditTool at all.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Write a new module that re-implements per-manager argv construction (duplicating auditArgv's logic, which is module-private and not exported from pkg/index.ts) and calls runShell directly with full control over cwd/env/proxy from the start, never touching pkgAuditTool's existing execute() path.
pros: Total control over every invocation detail from the first line, no coordination with pkg_audit's existing input/output shape at all
cons: Directly violates ac2's explicit text: 'implemented as the EvidenceProvider registry's dependency-sbom category wired to the existing pkg_audit tool ..., not a new fetcher' -- this alternative IS a new fetcher
Duplicates per-manager argv logic (auditArgv) that already exists and is already correct, doubling the maintenance surface for npm/pnpm/yarn/pip/pipenv/poetry/go/cargo argument shapes
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac2's explicit text outright by being exactly the 'new fetcher' the Story forbids, and duplicates auditArgv's already-correct per-manager logic -- rejected regardless of its other merits.

alternativesConsidered.name: Mutate the daemon's own process.env around the pkg_audit call
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Avoid changing pkg_audit's code at all by temporarily overwriting process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY (and restoring it afterward) for the duration of the call, since pkgAuditTool.execute defaults to process.env when no env override is passed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Before calling pkgAuditTool.execute, set process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY to the ephemeral proxy's address and the manager's scoped settings; restore the prior values in a finally block after the call returns.
pros: Zero changes to pkg_audit's own source at all
cons: process.env is GLOBAL to the daemon's Node process, which the daemon's own threaded/session architecture runs concurrent, unrelated shell-backed tool calls inside (per the project's daemon.threads design) -- a security review's proxy env could leak onto, or be clobbered by, a completely unrelated concurrent shell call in the same process, a correctness and isolation hazard a1's per-call options.env entirely avoids

A restore-in-finally still has a window where a concurrent call on another async task sees the mutated environment, since Node's single-threaded event loop interleaves awaits -- this is not a theoretical risk given the daemon already runs many concurrent tool calls per session
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Nominally keeps ac2's wiring intact (same pkgAuditTool.execute call site, no schema change) but the enforcement mechanism itself is unsafe under the daemon's own concurrent, threaded session model -- a global process.env mutation is not a boundary sc2's 'enforced, not merely observed' advisoryDestination can rely on.
